To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the achievable capacity of a MIMO system depends on (i) the modulation scheme used at the transmitter, (ii) the number of transmit antennas, (iii) the number of receive antennas and (iv) the channel SNR.

the MIMO system designed with the aim of achieving full diversity gain can achieve higher capacity than the MIMO system with the aim of maximizing the multiplexing gain if the channel SNR value is sufficiently low.

transmit diversity can be used to narrow the gap between the MIMO capacity of a Rayleigh-fading MIMO channel and the AWGMIMO channel, and the performance advantage of using transmit diversity diminishes when the receiver diversity increases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of multi-dimensional signal constellations for MIMO channels and the evaluation of their capacity.
the design of MIMO systems for achieving full multiplexing and full diversity gains.

the evaluation of the capacity of the MIMO system using the following multi-dimensional signal sets: 1) the 2-dimensional QPSK, 2) the 3-dimensional 8PSK, 3) the 4-dimensional 16QAM, and 4) the 8-dimensional 64QAM.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
for the MIMO system with full multiplexing and full diversity gains, the capacity performance is better than that of a MIMO system having only one of those gains.
for high SNRs and low-order diversity, transmit diversity is preferable to receiver diversity.
transmit diversity is more suitable for the low to moderate SNR region, while receiver diversity is more appropriate for the high SNR region.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
transmit diversity is more beneficial than receiver diversity in MIMO systems.

for the Rayleigh-faded MIMO channel, the capacity is a function of the channel SNR, the diversity order of the system, the modulation scheme and the number of transmit as we ll as the number of receive antennas.
the capacity of MIMO systems is not only determined by the number of transmit and receive antennas, but also by the signal constellation used.
The main takeaway from our work is that
for a given number of transmit and receive antennas, the achievable capacity is maximized when the number of dimensions of the signal constellation is equal to the number of receive antennas.
the achievable capacity of a MIMO system depends on the channel SNR, the number of receive antennas, the modulation order, and the diversity order.
the capacity of MIMO systems using multi-dimensional constellations can be evaluated by means of a simple formula which does not require numerical integration.
